title: Workspace Purpose
applicability: Introduces the purpose of the 2D state-event procedure design workspace in BestNameYet/Terminals.
purpose: Design and document an MCP-based interactive procedure with nonce-keyed persistent execution records, keyword-addressed projection definitions and accepted inputs, deterministic transitions through state.next, two interactive queue phases, and a complete persisted run record. The same nonce identifies the current saved state and projection until that procedure terminates.

title: Machine-Dialect Requirements for Workspace Agent Instructions
applicability: Every current and future entry, including nested instructional members and examples, in workspaces/2d-state-event-procedure-design/AGENTS.json.
required_behavior: Write and interpret every entry in this AGENTS.json according to both the explicit requirements and the spirit of machine dialect: preserve complete intended behavioral meaning, describe scope and required actions unambiguously, and provide enough operational context for an agent to interpret each instruction without guessing. Apply the complete authoritative definition reproduced verbatim below, including all of its writing requirements, contrastive examples, and validation criteria.

title: Nonce-Persisted Procedure States and Keyword-Bound Return Schemas
applicability: Governs the design, implementation, extension, validation, execution, queuing, resumption, and testing of every procedure-machine state, event, step file, instruction and schema pair, transition handler, and associated context exchange developed in this workspace.

architectural_definition.dimensions: The execution state is identified by a procedure nonce and a semantic state keyword; no persistent numeric step index or keyword-index map is required. A keyword addresses a projection definition and its process handler independently of position.
architectural_definition.state: A nonce retrieves the active execution record, including state.keyword, state.next, its already generated state.projection with final_schema, and accepted inputs by keyword. A state handler generates a projection from an addressable definition and previously accepted keyword values, or validates new input against the saved final_schema.
architectural_definition.event: E_RETURN(input) is a separate agent submission after the projection has been rendered. It contains an object under exactly the current state keyword; its presence does not itself signify acceptance.
architectural_definition.function_pointer: The controller dispatches input processing by record.state.keyword to the corresponding state-specific handler. The projection builder resolves the keyword-addressed definition, process handler, and optional schema-derivation function reference; no steps[i] lookup is used.
architectural_definition.context_object: The nonce-persisted record.inputs stores previously accepted values by independent semantic keyword. Projection generation resolves required earlier values there. Each agent call submits only the current keyword, and a rejection diagnostic is attached to the current stored projection without a pending separate control state.
architectural_definition.transition: Validate the submitted input against record.state.projection.final_schema and applicable semantic constraints. On rejection, keep the current state and its unchanged instruction and final_schema, add a diagnostic, persist, and render. On acceptance, store record.inputs[state.keyword], generate the successor named by state.next, save the same nonce record, and render its projection. A null successor marks completion.
architectural_definition.initialization: Starting with no procedure arguments generates a unique nonce and the initial verbatim_request projection, saves the record, then renders the projection. Invoking with only an existing nonce returns the saved projection unchanged; invoking with nonce and input processes that current input.
architectural_definition.persistence_and_handoff: Persist the nonce, current state keyword and successor, full generated projection and final_schema, all accepted keyword values, and continuity across queue handoff, suspension, and resumption. Keep each procedure independent by nonce; do not recalculate the schema on replay.

mandatory_behavior.non_deviation: Every procedure state, input, validation, retry, rendering action and queue continuation must use the nonce-persisted execution record and keyword-addressed state definitions. Do not reintroduce indexed iterator advancement, persistent keyword index maps, agent-selected destinations, or rendering coupled to receiving input.
mandatory_behavior.schema_contracts: Present the complete instruction and concrete JSON return schema for the current keyword. The agent supplies only that keyword. The generated final_schema is stored in the nonce record and used unchanged for input validation and nonce-only replay.
mandatory_behavior.handler_contracts: The state-specific handler validates submitted input against the saved final_schema and its semantic requirements, returning validity and any diagnostic. Projection generation, not rendering, resolves prior accepted input and the schema-derivation function. The controller persists and selects the successor by state.next.
mandatory_behavior.continuity: Accepted inputs must remain available as record.inputs[keyword] under independent stable addresses. Later procedure, simulation, execution and diagnostic representations preserve their original change-to-action associations and decorate them rather than creating disconnected lists.
mandatory_behavior.prohibited_substitution: Select the successor from the current saved state.next after acceptance, never by numeric index, input-supplied state name, or event column. A rejected input retains the same active state and final_schema.

dispatch_notation.table_cell: record.state.keyword is the current keyword and record.state.next is its successor keyword or null.
dispatch_notation.invocation: f(agentInput, nonce, {load,save,render}) loads the execution record; with no input it replays the saved projection, and with input it validates and saves either a diagnostic retry or the generated successor.
dispatch_notation.interpretation: Step order is expressed by keyword-addressed next references; a keyword permanently identifies the corresponding full instruction, return schema and applicable validator regardless of physical file placement.

examples.title: Initialization and accepted first return
sequence: A no-argument Procedure invocation creates a nonce and the initial verbatim_request state projection, persists it, then returns that projection.
The agent submits {verbatim_request: ...} with the same nonce in a later invocation.
The handler validates the saved final_schema, the controller records the accepted value and generates user_intent from state.next under the same nonce.

examples.title: Rejected input stays at the same index
sequence: With record.state.keyword equal to clarifying_questions, the agent submits an invalid clarifying_questions value.
The state-specific handler rejects the input and supplies a structured diagnostic.
The controller attaches the diagnostic to the same stored projection, preserves the unchanged instruction and final_schema, saves the record, and renders it again.

examples.title: Read accepted values by keyword
sequence: The nonce record stores accepted verbatim_request and user_intent values under their original keywords.
The clarifying_questions projection builder retrieves those values by keyword from record.inputs.
A validated reply adds only the clarifying_questions value to the same record.

examples.title: Simulation validation
sequence: The simulation_results projection is generated using execution_procedure and desired_state read by keyword.
Its final_schema, including derived constraints, is persisted before rendering.
A later nonce-plus-input invocation validates the stored schema and either persists a diagnostic retry or generates execution_results.

examples.title: Queue continuation
sequence: The application preserves the nonce-keyed record, previously accepted values, complete current projection, and history as required for queue handoff.
The resumed agent calls the procedure with its nonce and receives the identical current projection.
Its subsequent nonce-plus-input response is validated against the stored final_schema before advancing through state.next.

conformance_test: Conformance requires nonce-keyed persistence of the complete current projection and accepted inputs, full keyword-addressed instructions and schemas, state-specific validation against saved final_schema, deterministic state.next transitions, same-state diagnostic retry, and unchanged nonce-only replay.

title: State Tool-Response Input Instructions and JSON Return-Schema Alignment
applicability: Every projection returned to an agent by the nonce-based MCP procedure, including initialization, nonce-only replay, retry after rejected input, queued resumption and both interactive phases.

model_definition.state_meaning: A current execution record contains state.keyword, state.next and an already generated projection with instruction, final_schema, and resolved context. The projection is constructed before the agent responds, saved under the nonce and returned unchanged on nonce-only replay. Rejection adds a diagnostic to that saved projection; there is no separately pending diagnostic that a state function must capture and clear.
model_definition.expected_input: The agent separately returns an object containing only the keyword requested in the saved projection. Earlier accepted values remain under record.inputs[keyword], and retries request a corrected value under the same keyword and final_schema.
model_definition.two_required_presentations: Every saved projection renders two consistent presentations: (1) complete machine-dialect instruction sentences and (2) the concrete, syntactically valid final_schema as JSON. Their full source definitions are externally addressable by keyword; projection generation resolves them and any derivation reference before persistence. The renderer outputs the already generated content without deriving or loading new state.
model_definition.input_contract_boundary: The no-argument call generates and saves the first projection. A nonce-only call retrieves and renders the exact saved projection. A later nonce-plus-input call routes input to the current state validator, which uses the stored final_schema. Successful validation builds and persists a successor projection before rendering it.

mandatory_behavior.machine_dialect_statement: For each state, generate a sentence-form instruction applying machine-dialect requirements to identify the input being requested, the values the agent must derive or preserve, their relationships to earlier accepted values referenced by keyword, and any relevant cardinality, identity, ordering, or allowed-value constraints. The statement must be sufficiently complete for an agent to construct the requested return without inferring undocumented meanings.
mandatory_behavior.valid_json_return_schema: In the same rendered tool response, display a real, syntactically valid JSON return schema as JSON, not pseudo-JSON, TypeScript notation, abbreviated field declarations, or an unexplained example payload. The schema must specify the expected object structure, data types, required properties, and applicable structural constraints so the submitted agent return can be validated.
mandatory_behavior.mandatory_sentence_for_every_nontrivial_: For every non-trivial key present anywhere in the JSON return schema, including nested object properties and array-item properties, the machine-dialect instruction statement must include at least one complete sentence explaining that key's intended value and expected input shape. The explanation must state what belongs in the field, not merely repeat the field name or JSON type. For worked examples illustrating complete sentence-form explanations of schema keys, including nested object properties and array-item properties, use the state instruction and return-schema pairs in the referenced workspace file: https://github.com/BestNameYet/Terminals/blob/main/workspaces/2d-state-event-procedure-design/state-instructions-and-return-schemas.json. The referenced examples illustrate this requirement and do not replace the instruction or schema for the current runtime state.
mandatory_behavior.cross_representation_alignment: The machine-dialect statement and the displayed JSON return schema must describe the same expected agent input. Every required field, nested relationship, array size limitation, enumeration, identifier reference, and other significant schema constraint must be represented consistently in the statement; no statement may request a structurally incompatible return and no schema may silently impose an unexplained non-trivial requirement.
mandatory_behavior.full_context_preservation: Require only the current keyword in the final_schema. Resolve prior accepted values from record.inputs by keyword during projection generation. On retry retain the complete unchanged instruction and final_schema while adding the validation diagnostic to the saved projection.
mandatory_behavior.validation_responsibility: The state-specific input-processing function validates the submitted value against the already persisted final_schema and applicable semantic constraints. A missing required prior accepted value during new projection generation is an implementation error rather than an input rejection.
mandatory_behavior.nonconformance: A rendered state is nonconforming when it omits either required input presentation, displays invalid JSON as the return schema, leaves a non-trivial schema key without a sentence-form explanation, or gives machine-dialect and schema definitions that disagree. Correct the rendered state contract before treating it as an acceptable procedure-machine state.
mandatory_behavior.instruction_schema_pair: Address each complete instruction and base schema by one semantic keyword in the reference. During projection generation resolve that pair, required previously accepted values and the optional derivation function to form the concrete final_schema; store the result under the nonce before rendering. Validate the later input only against that persisted final_schema. No schema derivation or reference lookup occurs during replay or presentation.

examples.title: Clarifying questions use one keyword
examples.rendered_machine_dialect_instruction: Read `verbatim_request` and `user_intent`. Return `clarifying_questions` as an array of 7–11 questions necessary to fulfill the request. Each `id` is a unique stable question identifier such as Q1. Each `question` is a complete interrogative sentence.

displayed_json_return_schema.description: Response object containing the current state input under the semantic keyword clarifying_questions. Earlier accepted inputs remain in the nonce-persisted execution record, addressed by keyword.

clarifying_questions.description: The `clarifying_questions` property is an array containing between seven and eleven question objects needed to fulfill the user request.

items.description: Each object in `clarifying_questions` represents one question and contains its identifier and full question text.

id.description: The `clarifying_questions[].id` property is a string uniquely identifying the question, such as Q1.

question.description: The `clarifying_questions[].question` property is a string containing a complete interrogative sentence identifying information needed to fulfill the request.

examples.implementation_interpretation: The projection builder retrieves verbatim_request and user_intent from record.inputs by keyword and persists the complete clarifying_questions projection, including final_schema. A later nonce-plus-input call validates the submitted clarifying_questions and checks identifier uniqueness in addition to JSON Schema validation.

examples.title: Nonconforming unexplained nested key
examples.explanation: This example violates the rule because the sentence does not explain what execution_order means, how the integer relates to other steps, or what the identifiers in action_ids reference. These meanings must be explained in complete sentences alongside the schema.

title: Deterministic Nonce-Based State Transitions and Context Argument Passing
applicability: Every transition, agent-submitted input, keyword-addressed previous value, projection generation, validation retry and queue continuation in the nonce-persisted interactive procedure.

definitions.ordered_deterministic_route: The current nonce record contains the active state and its successor keyword state.next. Acceptance generates and persists the successor; rejection retains the state and adds a diagnostic without changing its final_schema. A null successor denotes completion.
definitions.agent_event: E_RETURN(input) is the subsequent nonce-plus-input submission, containing only the current state keyword and value; it does not determine validity or a destination.
definitions.context_address: An accepted input is stored in record.inputs under its semantic keyword. For example, record.inputs.verbatim_request holds the accepted original prompt.
definitions.selected_function: The current state keyword selects its validation handler; the projection builder resolves the next keyword definition and optional derivation function using the projection reference.
definitions.state_arguments: Give the validator access to the persisted final_schema and the current run's accepted values by keyword. Give projection generation only its declared prerequisite inputs. Rendering receives the complete already-built projection.

mandatory_behavior.deterministic_transition_order: On valid input, persist record.inputs[state.keyword], generate the keyword named in state.next, and persist the new projection under the same nonce before rendering. On invalid input, retain the current state, attach the diagnostic and render its unchanged instruction and final_schema.
mandatory_behavior.agent_input_drives_events: Treat the agent response in a separate nonce-plus-input invocation as the event payload. The agent supplies the current keyword and value; the application validates it and chooses the result, never the agent.
mandatory_behavior.unique_specified_input_addresses: Assign each requested input a stable semantic keyword. Preserve earlier accepted values in record.inputs under their existing keywords.
mandatory_behavior.function_event_argument: Deliver E_RETURN(input) to the handler selected by the current persisted state.keyword; validate with its final_schema and applicable semantic constraints while resolving required prior values from record.inputs.
mandatory_behavior.function_controls_next_state: The handler controls acceptance or rejection, not the destination. The controller follows persisted state.next only after acceptance; rejected input cannot advance or change the keyword.
mandatory_behavior.state_receives_derived_arguments: During new projection construction resolve only the declared prior keyword inputs and schema-derivation function. Do not derive a schema when validating, replaying, or rendering; retain a rejection diagnostic on the saved projection.
mandatory_behavior.initial_invocation_contract: Create and save the initial verbatim_request projection when called without a procedure argument. On nonce-only resumption load and return the saved projection without recalculation.

examples.title: Accepted input advances exactly once
sequence: The initial no-argument invocation persists the verbatim_request projection under a newly generated nonce.
The agent later submits its verbatim_request input with that nonce and the handler validates the saved final_schema.
The controller saves the accepted value and generates user_intent from the current state.next.

examples.title: Validation retry does not change event type
sequence: The clarifying_questions state receives invalid input through its nonce.
The state-specific handler returns rejection and a diagnostic.
The controller saves the same state and adds the diagnostic to the projection before rendering it again, with its instruction and final_schema unchanged.

examples.title: Previous values remain available by keyword
sequence: The question_answers projection builder retrieves clarifying_questions from the nonce record by keyword.
It derives the concrete final_schema from the accepted questions, persists the state and renders the projection.
A subsequent call validates only question_answers against the saved final_schema and leaves earlier inputs intact.

conformance: The current nonce record selects a handler and stores the derived final_schema; separate input validation produces acceptance or a diagnostic; the controller follows state.next only on acceptance and replays the current saved projection unchanged when no input is supplied.
implementation_choice_status: Nonce-keyed persistent execution records and keyword-addressed projection definitions replace indexed iterator advancement and deferred state pointers. No additional step-index map or pending-diagnostic state is part of the active contract.

title: State-Event Handler Invocation and Explicit Stored-State Arguments
applicability: Every dispatch of agent input using a nonce, schema validation against a saved projection, same-state diagnostic retry, and successor generation for the interactive procedure.

architectural_contract.intersection_selection: The nonce retrieves the current execution record, whose state.keyword determines the corresponding state-specific processing handler.
architectural_contract.event_consumption: The processing handler receives the agent input and may read earlier accepted inputs by keyword from the same nonce record.
architectural_contract.validation: Validate against the saved state.projection.final_schema and applicable semantic constraints; return true with accepted input or false with a structured diagnostic.
architectural_contract.invalid_response_route: On rejection, preserve the current keyword, its unchanged instruction and final_schema, attach the diagnostic to its projection, save under the same nonce and render the retry.
architectural_contract.valid_response_route: On acceptance, save the keyword value, generate the next projection by state.next using declared prior inputs and schema derivation, save under the same nonce, and render; a null successor completes the procedure.
architectural_contract.functional_argument_passing: Use a run-scoped keyword lookup for accepted values, and pass the already generated final_schema into validation. Diagnostics are part of the saved projection, not an independent pending input.
architectural_contract.startup_defaults: A no-argument invocation creates a nonce and initial verbatim_request projection; nonce-only resumption renders that saved projection.
architectural_contract.deferred_or_immediate_invocation: The renderer never collects agent input. Input arrives in a later invocation of the same procedure nonce, whose controller dispatches the current handler and saves the resulting state.

mandatory_behavior.deterministic_selection: Choose the processing handler by persisted state.keyword. It determines validity from the agent input and persisted final_schema, not from an agent-supplied Boolean. The agent cannot choose the successor.
mandatory_behavior.schema_validation_and_retry: Validate the current keyword against the saved final_schema. A rejected reply leaves the active state and schema unchanged, with an additional diagnostic saved in the projection.
mandatory_behavior.separate_context_and_state_argument: Expose the accepted keyword values to projection generation and state-specific validation without returning a complete context object to the agent. Give the renderer only the stored projection.
mandatory_behavior.no_global_state_dependency: All previous-value lookups and active-state selection are scoped to the nonce. Do not use global current indices or separate pending-error slots.
mandatory_behavior.initial_state_defaults: A new run starts with a new nonce, empty accepted keyword inputs and the generated verbatim_request projection; resumption loads the stored record without rebuilding its final_schema.

examples.title: One state callable uses a separate renderer
examples.explanation: The example illustrates structural validation against the stored schema; a real handler additionally applies all state-specific semantic checks. The renderer is not invoked by the handler and cannot collect input.

examples.title: Controller follows the saved successor keyword after acceptance
examples.explanation: The controller persists the new projection or the same-state retry before rendering. A null state.next marks completion instead of calling buildState.

conformance: A nonce loads one current state and saved final_schema. Its handler validates input, and the controller persists either the same-state diagnostic projection or the keyword-defined successor projection before rendering.

title: Agent Return and Accepted Inputs by Keyword
applicability: Applies to agent input submitted with a procedure nonce and to previously accepted keyword values persisted in the same nonce execution record.

requirements.title: Event representation
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the agent submission as E_RETURN(input) in a separate nonce-plus-input invocation. Its object contains only the current state keyword and corresponding value; the event does not include validation status or a requested next state.

requirements.title: Unique input addresses
requirements.required_behavior: Assign each independently recallable input a stable semantic keyword. Store it as record.inputs[keyword] and resolve declared prior inputs by keyword when building a new projection.

requirements.title: Context accumulation
requirements.required_behavior: After validation against the saved final_schema and semantic rules, persist the accepted value by keyword under the same nonce. Preserve all earlier accepted values. Keep rejection diagnostics in the current stored projection rather than treating them as accepted inputs or as a separate pending state.

requirements.title: Property ownership
requirements.required_behavior: Document the one keyword expected at each state. The projection builder resolves its complete instruction and derived final_schema before persistence; the state-specific handler later validates the agent return against that same stored schema. Rendering never receives agent input.

example.title: Keyword-addressed agent replies
sequence: A new Procedure call returns a nonce and saved verbatim_request projection.
The agent submits {verbatim_request: ...} with that nonce; the handler validates the stored final_schema and record.inputs.verbatim_request is saved.
The controller builds and saves user_intent using state.next and the accepted original prompt.
The agent separately returns {user_intent: ...} with the same nonce; the handler validates it and record.inputs.user_intent is stored independently.

title: File-Level Change Mapping as the Procedure's Structural Foundation
applicability: The procedure-design phase that compares the current system state with the user-requested desired final system state, identifies filesystem changes, identifies agent actions, maps the actions to those changes, and subsequently expands the mappings into a procedure.
purpose: Ensure that the procedure specifies concrete, individually identifiable file changes and the agent actions that produce each change, rather than producing an abstract action list disconnected from the desired final state.

required_behavior.file_level_granularity: For each filesystem transformation required by the desired final system state, describe the change at the level of the specific file affected. Give each separately identifiable file change its own change identifier, specify the affected file path, and classify its operation as create, modify, or delete. Do not substitute a broad directory-level or project-level description when a specific file change can be identified.
required_behavior.desired_state_traceability: Identify which required condition or conditions of the desired final system state each file-level change is intended to satisfy. Preserve these relationships using the existing identifiers assigned to the final-state requirements and changes.
required_behavior.actions_per_change: For each defined file change, identify the exact agent action or actions needed to produce that change. Map the action identifiers to the corresponding file-change identifier so the procedure can independently recover which actions effect which file changes. An action may be referenced by multiple change mappings where it produces multiple independently identified file changes.
required_behavior.mapping_as_skeleton: Treat the existing change-to-action mappings as the canonical skeleton of the procedure. When generating ordered steps, command examples, code examples, simulation outputs, execution observations, or diagnostics, extend or decorate those mappings without replacing them with an unrelated action list, dropping original identifiers, or losing the link to the desired final state.
required_behavior.completion_coverage: Represent every required file-level change in the mapping and associate it with its necessary actions. Where a required file change or action remains unmapped, identify the gap rather than silently omitting the requirement.

example.scenario: The user's desired final state requires adding a new JSON configuration file and modifying an existing JavaScript program to read it.

actions.description: Write the required configuration data to config/settings.json.
Modify src/app.js so it reads config/settings.json and uses the configured values.

example.interpretation: The two file changes remain separately addressable and traceable to the desired final-state conditions. Subsequent procedure and simulation stages add execution details to these same mappings rather than replacing them.

title: Two-Phase Interactive MCP Procedure Queue and Agent Handoff
applicability: The two-phase interactive MCP workflow that creates a procedure with a first agent, queues it, and resumes the same nonce-persisted run with a second agent for review, execution and post-execution diagnostics.
purpose: Establish that both sides of the queued handoff are interactive procedures, not an issue-comment job processor or an offline batch execution, so future queue design and implementation preserve the intended agent-facing MCP interaction.

required_behavior.first_phase_interactive_procedure: The first agent starts with a no-argument call that generates a nonce and initial projection. Each subsequent nonce-plus-input call validates the current keyword against the saved final_schema and substantive rules. Acceptance generates the state.next projection; rejection saves an additive diagnostic on the same projection. The agent identifies changes, maps actions, builds a procedure, and simulates commands, code and predicted effects.
required_behavior.queue_handoff: After procedure preparation, queue the prepared procedure together with the existing nonce and access to its persisted record.inputs and current complete projection. Preserve file-change identifiers, action identifiers, mapping, schema and accepted data for the second agent; do not start an unrelated execution record.
required_behavior.second_phase_interactive_procedure: The second agent retrieves the queued nonce and replays the same stored projection. Its subsequent nonce-plus-input calls review and execute the prepared procedure, and complete post-execution diagnostics against the original desired state and checklist. Each submitted state is validated against its saved schema and semantic rules; state.next controls advancement.
required_behavior.mcp_based_queue: Expose the queue and both interactive procedure phases through the application's MCP-based interface. Treat IssueStack's issue-backed queue only as historical design context, not as a required implementation or an execution dependency; an Issue-comment-triggered workflow is not a substitute for the intended interactive MCP queue.
required_behavior.preserve_machine_architecture: Across queue transport, assignment, suspension, resumption and phase transfer preserve the nonce, current keyword, successor, complete stored projection with final_schema, accepted inputs by keyword, mapped file/action identities and deterministic retry/transition behavior. Do not persist or reconstruct a numeric iterator index.
required_behavior.retain_full_run: Ensure the application's complete run record encompasses both interactive phases, the queue handoff, actual execution results, and post-execution diagnostics. The queue must preserve continuity of the same procedure rather than treating the second phase as a new unrelated request.

example.title: Interactive procedure authoring followed by interactive review and execution
sequence: Agent 1 starts a procedure and responds to each saved projection using its nonce; the active state-specific handler validates each keyword submission.
Agent 1 produces a file-level change-to-action mapping and decorates that mapping with the stepwise procedure and a proposed simulation containing commands, code and predicted effects.
The application queues the prepared procedure and its existing nonce, retaining accepted inputs, identifiers, mappings and current projection.
Agent 2 uses the same nonce to replay the saved projection, then submits the current keyword under that nonce to continue the same run.
Agent 2 executes the reviewed procedure and interactively supplies actual execution observations and the decorated post-execution diagnostic checklist.
The application retains the complete record spanning both agents and the handoff.

implementation_boundary: The requirement specifies interactive queue behavior and continuity, not queue storage format, claim protocol, scheduling policy, or MCP tool name. The selected runtime architecture does fix the persistence of current projection and accepted keyword inputs under a reusable nonce; other queue design choices remain unspecified.

title: Runner, Keyword State Selection, Stored Projection Renderer, and Two Interactive Applications
applicability: Architecture of the MCP-based procedure system, including starting a procedure, resolving step transitions, presenting state instructions, creating queued procedures, reviewing and executing queued jobs, post-execution review, and access to completed jobs.

runner.purpose: Coordinate no-argument procedure creation, nonce-only projection replay, nonce-plus-input processing, persistence and the two interactive applications.
runner.required_behavior: Create a nonce and first state projection, or load the existing nonce record. Validate input against the saved final_schema through its state-specific handler; save accepted inputs by keyword and generate state.next on acceptance, or save a diagnostic on the same projection on rejection.
runner.expected_interface: Use create(nonce, {save,render}) for initialization and f(agentInput, nonce, {load,save,render}) for processing or replay. The interactive MCP alias supplies the nonce and optional input.

state_event_dispatcher.purpose: Resolve the current state-specific processing handler by record.state.keyword.
state_event_dispatcher.required_behavior: For a nonce-plus-input call, dispatch once to the current handler using its saved final_schema and declared previously accepted inputs. Never derive schema or render during input validation.
state_event_dispatcher.expected_interface: Load the current state and look up its handler by semantic keyword; use state.next solely for accepted transitions.

state_object_construction.purpose: Generate a complete, persistable state and projection from keyword-addressed definitions.
state_object_construction.required_behavior: The projection builder resolves declared earlier accepted values, complete instruction, base JSON Schema and optional schema derivation function; it builds the concrete final_schema and projection exactly once for the new active state and saves them under the nonce before rendering.
state_object_construction.expected_interface: buildState(keyword, inputs) resolves the appropriate keyword-addressed reference and returns state.keyword, state.next, and the generated projection with instruction, final_schema and required context.

renderer.purpose: Present the already saved projection as an agent-facing MCP response.
renderer.required_behavior: Output the persisted full instruction and concrete final_schema without resolving definitions, deriving a schema, collecting input or modifying transitions. On validation failure, conspicuously present the additive saved diagnostic before unchanged normal instruction and schema.
renderer.expected_interface: Accept the complete saved projection and return or emit it without changing its content. Projection configuration lookup belongs to the builder, not the renderer.

applications.minimum_separation: Implement at least two distinct applications using the shared procedure architecture. They must not be collapsed into a single indistinguishable workflow that obscures the two interactive queue phases.

procedure_creation_application.purpose: Provide the interactive application through which an agent creates a procedure to satisfy a user request.
procedure_creation_application.required_behavior: Start a nonce-persisted procedure, render successive stored projections, accept separate nonce-plus-input submissions, derive file-level changes and mapped agent actions, and build and simulate the procedure. At handoff queue the existing nonce and prepared procedure with complete accepted context and mappings.

job_review_execution_application.purpose: Provide the interactive application through which an agent accesses queued jobs, inspects their prepared procedures, carries out their actions, performs post-execution review, and accesses completed jobs.
job_review_execution_application.required_behavior: List queued jobs, select an existing nonce-persisted procedure, replay its current projection, and interactively process review, execution and post-execution input with saved final_schema validation. Complete jobs only under the defined completion conditions; retain results and access to completed jobs.

responsibility_boundaries.responsibility: Coordinate procedure startup, nonce-based replay, independent agent input processing, state.next transitions, persistence, queue handoff and interactive application lifecycle.
Load and save the complete current execution record; validate against saved final_schema through the selected state handler; follow state.next only after success; attach diagnostics on rejection.
Resolve the current validation handler, state successor and schema-derivation reference by semantic keyword; never maintain a persistent numeric index.
Validate the submitted current-keyword object against the saved final_schema and substantive constraints; return acceptance and input or a structured diagnostic.

Read required accepted values by keyword, resolve full externally configured instruction and schema, optionally derive the concrete final_schema, and construct the successor projection before persistence.
Render the saved complete projection and any additive diagnostic; do not resolve references, derive schema, validate input or choose transitions.
Display queued and completed jobs and interactively review, execute, diagnose and complete jobs.

illustrative_flow: A no-argument procedure invocation creates a nonce, resolves the initial keyword definition, generates its projection with concrete final_schema, persists the record and renders it.
A nonce-only invocation loads and returns the exact previously generated projection without regenerating any reference or schema.
In a separate nonce-plus-input invocation, the current state handler validates the agent's one-keyword input against its persisted final_schema and applicable semantic constraints.
On rejection the controller adds an externally configured diagnostic to the existing projection, persists it, and renders the same full instruction and final_schema.

On acceptance the controller saves record.inputs[state.keyword], constructs the successor specified by state.next using prior keyword inputs, persists the same nonce record, then renders the generated projection.
The procedure-creation application queues the prepared procedure and the existing nonce, with accepted values and mappings intact.
The review/execution application resumes that nonce and continues the interactive execution and post-execution diagnostic phase before publishing completed jobs.
unresolved_implementation_decisions: Do not infer additional queue scheduling, claim, ownership, completion-status or UI protocols. The selected architecture specifies a nonce-keyed persistent execution record, keyword-addressed projection references, saved final_schema validation and output-only rendering; the two distinct interactive applications remain required.

title: External Addressable Content and Reference-Only Rendering
applicability: Every script, module, state function, transition function, runner, dispatcher, renderer, and interactive application that creates or displays agent-facing tool responses or other system-generated interface text in this workspace.
purpose: Separate all rendered wording and configurable display content from executable scripts. Every displayed instruction, prompt, label, diagnostic, explanatory sentence, or other system-authored text must be stored in independently addressable configuration resources rather than hardcoded in program source.

definitions.rendered_text: Any system-authored text that a program causes the agent or job viewer to see, including state instructions, return-schema explanations, validation errors, display headings, labels, queue/job prompts and completion diagnostics. Dynamically echoed agent inputs or observed command output are runtime data, not hardcoded display templates.
definitions.external_content_resource: A configuration file outside the executable script that stores content entries under stable addresses or keys. The exact file paths, format, and organization are not specified by this requirement.
definitions.content_reference: A stable semantic keyword or keyed reference that the projection builder uses to resolve the complete external instruction, base schema, derivation function and diagnostic templates. The saved projection contains their resolved results for output-only rendering.
definitions.rendering_resolution: Projection generation resolves externally configured instruction and schema references, derives a concrete final_schema and saves the complete projection under the nonce. The separate renderer outputs that saved projection without new lookups, substitutions or derivation.

mandatory_behavior.absolute_prohibition_on_embedded_render_: Do not hardcode, declare, concatenate, interpolate, or store any system-authored rendered text directly inside an executable script. A script may contain identifiers, references, control flow, field names, and runtime data operations; it must not carry the user-facing wording that those identifiers select.
mandatory_behavior.external_configurable_storage: Store every system-authored rendered text value in an addressable, configurable file located outside the executable script. Each value must have a uniquely specified reference that the application can resolve when needed. Updating display wording must be possible through the configuration resource without editing executable script source.
mandatory_behavior.reference_only_state_objects: Generated state records contain state.keyword, state.next, a complete persisted projection with externally sourced instruction and concrete final_schema, and optionally an additive diagnostic. State generation must resolve references before saving and rendering. The executable script must not hardcode system-authored display wording.
mandatory_behavior.reference_only_diagnostics: On failed validation the state handler returns a structured error with errortype and data. The controller resolves its externally configured diagnostic text when adding error_message to the already saved projection; the same instruction and final_schema remain unchanged, and no separate pending error state or clear-on-next-render lifecycle is introduced.
mandatory_behavior.renderer_resolves_references: The projection builder, not the renderer, resolves external instruction, schema and diagnostic references. The renderer outputs the already persisted normal instruction and final_schema, plus any resolved additive diagnostic before them. Missing references fail projection construction or diagnostic augmentation, never trigger invented fallback text.
mandatory_behavior.all_applications_in_scope: Apply the same reference-only rendering rule to both the interactive procedure-creation application and the queued-job review/execution/completion application. This includes job lists, job selection, completed-job displays and post-execution review wording.
mandatory_behavior.external_schema_content: Store base JSON Schemas and explanatory text in external addressable configuration. Resolve them by current keyword during projection generation; apply any referenced schema-derivation function to declared accepted prior values to persist the concrete final_schema. Scripts may implement constraint derivation but may not embed rendered schema explanations.
mandatory_behavior.preserve_machine_dialect: Externally stored state instructions must still satisfy the machine-dialect writing rules, describe every non-trivial schema key in sentence form, and align with the referenced valid JSON return schema. Moving content into configuration does not relax the state-input contract.

example.title: Builder resolves external content and saved projection is rendered unchanged
example.interpretation: The builder obtains system-authored content from the external reference and derives the concrete schema before the projection is persisted. The renderer receives and outputs the saved projection without recomputation. Rejection adds a resolved externally configured diagnostic before re-rendering the same instruction and schema.

implementation_boundary: This entry requires reference-only external content and output-only rendering of complete previously generated projections. The selected nonce-based runtime fixes the boundary between builder and renderer, but leaves content file formats, loaders, caching and presentation formatting implementation choices open.

title: State-Specific Validation Functions and Nonce-Controlled State Processing
applicability: Every keyword-addressed state handler, its input validation, rejection diagnostic, accepted value and current nonce-record transition in both interactive procedure applications.
architecture_decision: Each state has a keyword-addressed processing handler that validates a later nonce-plus-input submission against the exact final_schema already saved in the current projection and applies its semantic requirements. The controller handles persistence, diagnostic retry, and state.next advancement; the projection builder handles schema derivation before rendering.

mandatory_behavior.dedicated_handler_per_cell: Each semantic keyword has a handler that validates the submitted one-keyword input against the precise saved final_schema for that current state. A shared JSON Schema validator may check that pair without a numeric step position. Preserve state-specific identifier, coverage and mapping validation.
mandatory_behavior.invalid_input: On schema or semantic validation failure, return false and a structured diagnostic with an externally configured type and details. The controller retains the same state, adds the diagnostic to its projection, saves and renders it without a pending-error state.
mandatory_behavior.accepted_input: On successful validation, return true and the accepted one-keyword input. The controller stores it in record.inputs under that keyword and builds the next state from state.next, retaining the same nonce.
mandatory_behavior.state_builds_not_renders: The projection-generation function resolves keyword definitions and prior accepted inputs, applies an optional referenced schema-derivation function, and builds the full projection before it is saved and rendered. Validation occurs later against the saved final_schema; the processing handler does not call the renderer to solicit input.
mandatory_behavior.renderer_outputs_state_object: The renderer displays the already saved projection with complete unchanged instruction and final_schema. On rejection it presents the additive diagnostic first. It neither validates, builds a schema nor chooses the successor.
mandatory_behavior.preserve_reference_only_text: All displayed state instructions, error messages, base schema content, labels and formatting are externally configured. State handlers and projection generators use semantic identifiers and data operations without embedding system-authored displayed wording.
mandatory_behavior.procedure_specific_behavior: Each handler applies its existing substantive requirements, including cross-keyword checks, to the input and saved final_schema. Its Boolean determines acceptance; only the controller uses state.next for transition after acceptance.

illustrative_example.purpose: A clarifying_questions input arrives after its nonce-projection has been generated and rendered; the handler validates against the saved final_schema and produces a result without invoking the renderer.
illustrative_example.interpretation: The example preserves structural and semantic validation separately. The nonce controller, not this validation handler, saves accepted values, generates the keyword-addressed successor or saves an additive diagnostic, and renders only the persisted projection.

implementation_selection: Nonce-controlled state processing with keyword-addressed projections and state.next transitions supersedes zero-based indexed advancement and synchronous render-and-input handlers. The complete existing state-specific validation requirements remain mandatory.

title: Nonce-Persisted Procedure Controller, Validation Branching, and Additive Retry Rendering
applicability: Every no-argument procedure initialization, nonce replay, separate nonce-plus-input event, validation, successful keyword transition, same-state retry and queue continuation in this workspace.
purpose: Define deterministic persistence of one current state and complete generated projection per nonce, with keyword-addressed input retrieval, schema derivation at state generation, and additive validation diagnostics on rejection.

definitions.iterator_index: A numeric iterator index is not used for execution or persistence. The persistent nonce identifies a procedure record with one current state; its state.keyword and state.next identify the current and successor definitions.
definitions.context_object: The record.inputs object stores every previously accepted input under its stable semantic keyword. Only declared prerequisite keys are resolved during new projection generation.
definitions.state_function: The projection builder resolves the current keyword definition, complete instruction, base return schema and optional derive_schema function, constructing a concrete persisted projection with final_schema.
definitions.validation_function: After a separate nonce-plus-input call, the state-specific handler validates that input against the currently saved projection.final_schema and applicable semantic requirements, returning validity and any diagnostic.
definitions.validation_boolean: The Boolean is the application's acceptance result, not an agent-chosen event type or destination. Validity selects acceptance and state.next advancement, or rejection and same-state retry.
definitions.error_property: A validation failure is represented by a structured diagnostic containing error=true, errortype and diagnostic data; the controller attaches it to the saved current projection without a separate pending diagnostic state.
definitions.normal_mode: The saved projection's complete normal instruction and JSON final_schema are rendered without recomputation.
definitions.error_mode: The same saved projection is rendered with a conspicuous additive error_message before its otherwise unchanged normal instruction and final_schema.

mandatory_behavior.initialization: A procedure invocation without arguments creates a new nonce, builds the initial verbatim_request projection, persists the complete execution record and then returns the projection.
mandatory_behavior.state_invocation: For nonce-only invocation load and render the stored projection unchanged. For nonce-plus-input invocation dispatch to the processing handler identified by the saved state.keyword.
mandatory_behavior.error_detection: A submitted invalid input, as determined by the handler using the persisted final_schema and semantic checks, selects additive diagnostic retry on the current state. Absence of input selects exact replay, not an error mode decision.
mandatory_behavior.error_snapshot_and_reset: On rejection, add the diagnostic directly to the current saved projection, preserve its instruction and final_schema, and save the record before rendering. Do not create a separately pending error or clear the diagnostic by regenerating the state on the next replay.
mandatory_behavior.normal_rendering: Present the complete instruction and concrete final_schema already stored in record.state.projection; do not resolve the reference or derive schema during rendering.
mandatory_behavior.error_rendering: Present the structured externally resolved diagnostic conspicuously before the unchanged saved instruction and final_schema. The current state keyword and next pointer remain unchanged.
mandatory_behavior.agent_response: E_RETURN(input) arrives in a later invocation with the current nonce. Its object contains one requested keyword and value. The state-specific validator, not the agent, determines acceptance.
mandatory_behavior.function_selection: Select the processing handler by record.state.keyword; after successful validation resolve the successor definition from record.state.next. Do not use a persistent index, keyword map of numeric positions, or event column.
mandatory_behavior.input_validation: Validate the current one-keyword input against exactly record.state.projection.final_schema and all applicable state-specific semantic constraints.
mandatory_behavior.validation_success: On acceptance save record.inputs[state.keyword] and, if state.next is non-null, generate the next projection using declared previous keyword inputs and the referenced derivation function. Save under the same nonce before rendering. If state.next is null, persist completion.
mandatory_behavior.validation_failure: Return a structured error with error=true, errortype and diagnostic_data; preserve the current state and append its diagnostic to the saved projection for retry.
mandatory_behavior.index_retention: A rejected input retains the current state.keyword, state.next and final_schema under the nonce. It does not advance and does not require any index retention.
mandatory_behavior.boolean_transition: Use validation only to decide between same-state rejection and the deterministic keyword successor recorded as state.next. Do not compute i_next or i += Number(valid).
mandatory_behavior.recursive_continuation: After valid input build the successor by keyword and save it under the same nonce before rendering; each invocation requests only the current state's one semantic keyword.
mandatory_behavior.interaction_boundary: The renderer outputs the stored projection, ends the tool call, and does not await or solicit input. A subsequent nonce-plus-input invocation performs validation and may generate the next projection.
mandatory_behavior.context_preservation: Store all accepted inputs in record.inputs keyed by keyword. On rejection do not alter accepted values. New projection generation resolves only its declared prerequisite keywords.
mandatory_behavior.function_responsibility_boundary: The state-specific processing handler validates the current response and returns validity and diagnostic; the controller persists transitions or retries. The projection builder derives the schema before persistence; the renderer performs output only.
mandatory_behavior.renderer_responsibility_boundary: The renderer outputs complete saved projections and any already resolved additive diagnostic; it does not look up definitions, derive a schema, process inputs, change state.next, or decide error mode.
mandatory_behavior.persistence_and_handoff: Preserve nonce identity, current state keyword and successor, complete saved projection including final_schema, accepted inputs and required queue history across suspension and two-agent handoff.
mandatory_behavior.non_deviation: Do not reintroduce indexed iterator advancement, numeric keyword index maps, agent-selected destinations, validation-coded event types, synchronous render-and-reply exchange or a separate pending diagnostic state. Preserve full keyword definitions and substantive validator requirements.

interface_contracts.iterator_entry: create(nonce, {save,render}, initialKeyword) constructs, saves and renders the first state; f(agentInput, nonce, {load,save,render}) handles replay or submitted input.
interface_contracts.dispatch_entry: record.state.keyword identifies the active processing handler; state.next identifies the successor definition on acceptance.
interface_contracts.validation_return: The state-specific handler returns { valid, input, error }. valid is Boolean; input contains accepted one-keyword input on success and null on rejection; error contains diagnostic on failure and null on success.

failure_error_shape.errortype: Identifier for the externally configured diagnostic; structured diagnostic_data provides applicable validation details.

interface_contracts.index_update: No index update occurs. Valid input generates the successor named by state.next; invalid input preserves the current state and schema.
interface_contracts.continuation: Persist the generated successor projection or same-state diagnostic under the unchanged nonce, then render. A null state.next marks the run completed.

execution_examples.title: Initial successful validation
sequence: Start with a no-argument call, generate a nonce and persist the complete verbatim_request projection with no accepted inputs.
The agent separately submits {verbatim_request: ...} and the same nonce.
The handler validates against the stored final_schema and returns accepted input.
The controller saves record.inputs.verbatim_request, generates user_intent by state.next, saves and renders that projection.

execution_examples.title: Failed validation and same-state retry
sequence: A nonce-plus-input call submits invalid clarifying_questions.
The state-specific handler returns false with a structured diagnostic.
The controller retains the same state and schema and saves the diagnostic in the existing projection.
A nonce-only replay returns exactly that saved diagnostic projection.
The instruction and final_schema remain complete and unchanged.

execution_examples.title: Successful correction after retry
sequence: The agent sends corrected clarifying_questions with the existing nonce.
The handler validates the reply against the current stored final_schema and returns true.
The controller saves the accepted value by keyword, builds state.next, and the successor retrieves the accepted questions by keyword as needed.

relationship_to_existing_workspace_instr.preserved_requirements: Preserve complete external instructions and schemas, keyword-addressed accepted values, state-specific structural and semantic validation, deterministic transitions, persistent run records and the interactive two-phase queue.
relationship_to_existing_workspace_instr.superseded_transition_behavior: Separate projection generation, rendering and subsequent input validation. The controller follows state.next on acceptance or saves a diagnostic on the current projection on rejection.
relationship_to_existing_workspace_instr.superseded_index_convention: Use a persistent nonce, active state.keyword and state.next for execution; semantic keyword addresses accepted inputs and projection definitions.
relationship_to_existing_workspace_instr.reconciliation_requirement: Maintain one authoritative nonce-persisted execution contract across all instruction objects, examples and implementation; remove conflicting indexed-iterator and synchronous render-and-input contracts.

title: State Object Composition and Context-Derived Return Schemas
applicability: Every new keyword-addressed state projection generated for the nonce-based procedure, including the initial state and successors; rejected inputs reuse the saved projection with an additive diagnostic.
purpose: Specify complete persisted projection components and optional schema derivation from previously accepted keyword inputs, performed once during state generation before rendering.

definitions.state_object: The current nonce execution record contains state.keyword, state.next and state.projection. The projection is constructed and persisted before requesting agent input, and includes mandatory instruction and final_schema members plus conditional error_message after rejection.
definitions.instruction: The mandatory stored projection member containing the complete current-state machine-dialect instruction resolved from externally addressable keyword content, never hardcoded as display text in executable source.
definitions.return_schema: The required concrete JSON Schema is stored as projection.final_schema. It is obtained by cloning the externally configured base return_schema and optionally applying the referenced derivation function to declared accepted prior inputs at state generation time.
definitions.error_message: An optional additional diagnostic member attached to the already persisted current projection after input validation failure. It never replaces the original complete instruction or final_schema.
definitions.state_local_schema_helper: An optional per-state schema derivation function, referenced directly or by identifier in the keyword-addressed definition, that receives the base schema and explicitly declared accepted prior keyword values. It runs only when generating the new projection.

mandatory_behavior.mandatory_components: Each generated state projection must contain a complete instruction and concrete valid final_schema before it is persisted and rendered. Never substitute a schema placeholder or defer generation to rendering or validation.
mandatory_behavior.conditional_error_component: After a rejected nonce-plus-input event, attach error_message to the same stored projection and persist. With no rejection, omit this member. Do not introduce separate pending-error storage or capture-and-clear logic on replay.
mandatory_behavior.normal_and_error_composition: A normal saved projection includes instruction and final_schema. A rejected-state projection contains the same complete instruction and unchanged final_schema plus additive error_message displayed before them.
mandatory_behavior.instruction_content_source: The instruction member is resolved from external keyword-addressed content during projection generation. Generating or persisting the projection does not permit hardcoding system-authored instruction wording in executable source.
mandatory_behavior.schema_source_selection: At new state construction, obtain the externally configured base return_schema, apply any referenced derivation function using declared accepted input values, and persist the concrete syntactically valid final_schema. Replaying and rendering never regenerate it.
mandatory_behavior.optional_state_local_helper: A keyword state definition may reference a dedicated function that receives the base schema and explicitly identified accepted prior values by keyword; it computes final_schema before the projection is stored. Derivation is optional when the base schema alone suffices.
mandatory_behavior.context_derivation: Use only declared prior accepted values from the nonce record.inputs by keyword to derive schema fields, types, cardinalities, ordering and identifier constraints; do not alter earlier accepted values.
mandatory_behavior.schema_instruction_alignment: The persisted complete instruction and final_schema describe the same current one-keyword response. Any derived constraints come from accepted previous values; input validation uses precisely this saved final_schema.
mandatory_behavior.separate_rendering_responsibility: The builder creates the complete projection, the controller saves it, and the renderer outputs it unchanged. A later nonce-plus-input call invokes the appropriate validator. Rendering does not solicit input or resolve definitions.
mandatory_behavior.preserve_existing_architecture: The nonce record identifies the current state.keyword and its deterministic state.next successor. Saved final_schema controls acceptance; rejected input retains the current state and schema with an additive diagnostic. The external-content and two-phase queue obligations remain in force.

composition_examples.title: Normal state object

content_members.instruction: Complete resolved externally configured verbatim_request instruction

composition_examples.interpretation: Both mandatory members are generated and persisted under the nonce before rendering. No error_message exists because no rejection has occurred; schema is illustrative, not an instruction to hardcode a runtime schema.

composition_examples.title: Error-mode state object

content_members.instruction: The same complete resolved externally configured verbatim_request instruction
content_members.error_message: Resolved diagnostic added after rejected input

composition_examples.interpretation: Rejection adds an error_message to the saved current projection without rebuilding or changing instruction or final_schema. The renderer displays the diagnostic before the normal content.

composition_examples.title: State-local helper deriving a schema from context
composition_examples.interpretation: The builder reads accepted clarifying_questions by keyword, derives and persists the question_answers final_schema, then the renderer outputs the saved projection. A later nonce-plus-input call validates only question_answers against that saved final_schema.

conformance: A generated projection conforms when it contains the complete externally sourced instruction and valid concrete final_schema, adds error_message only as an unchanged-schema retry diagnostic, and uses declared keyword inputs for any schema derivation performed at generation time. No schema generation occurs during replay or rendering.
